import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the dataset
data = pd.read_csv('data/customer_segments.csv')

# Convert the Dt_Customer to datetime
data['Dt_Customer'] = pd.to_datetime(data['Dt_Customer'], format='%d-%m-%Y')

# Create a new column for the total spending on products
data['Total_Spending'] = data[['MntWines', 'MntFruits', 'MntMeatProducts', 
                               'MntFishProducts', 'MntSweetProducts', 'MntGoldProds']].sum(axis=1)

# Plot the relationship between Income and Total Spending
plt.figure(figsize=(10, 6))
sns.scatterplot(x='Income', y='Total_Spending', hue='Education', style='Marital_Status', data=data, alpha=0.7)

# Add labels and title

plt.ylabel('Total Spending')
plt.title('Income vs Total Spending by Education and Marital Status')

import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the dataset
data = pd.read_csv('data/customer_segments.csv')

# Convert the Dt_Customer to datetime
data['Dt_Customer'] = pd.to_datetime(data['Dt_Customer'], format='%d-%m-%Y')

# Create a new column for the total spending on products
data['Total_Spending'] = data[['MntWines', 'MntFruits', 'MntMeatProducts', 
                               'MntFishProducts', 'MntSweetProducts', 'MntGoldProds']].sum(axis=1)

# Plot the relationship between Income and Total Spending
plt.figure(figsize=(10, 6))
sns.scatterplot(x='Income', y='Total_Spending', hue='Education', style='Marital_Status', data=data, alpha=0.7)

# Add labels and title
plt.xlabel('Income')
plt.ylabel('Total Spending')
plt.title('Income vs Total Spending by Education and Marital Status')
